comments.text: The witch's shop's sprite shapes, 64 bytes each: memory_swap 2 exchanges $E000-$E4FF with $7B00-$7FFF when the shop opens ($EAF4) and again when it closes ($ECAB), so that these become sprite blocks $EC-$FF of bank 1. Blocks $EC-$FB ($E000-$E3FF) draw the witch (the raster routines shop_raster_witch_top and shop_raster_witch_low show eight each); the last 256 bytes hold two tablet icons and two screen layouts.
Sprite block $F5's shape, in the witch's sprites. The label is the engine's: $C954 calls $E240, the attract sequence's routine there, when the attract block is in.
Sprite block $FC once swapped in: the tablet icon for INFORMATION, a white i on a dark ground (f_259E's $FC, the ninth item the shop lists).
Sprite block $FD: the tablet icon for EXIT (f_259E's $FD).
24 character codes, a 6 x 4 block that shop_draw_panel draws at screen row 5, column 34 ($44EA), read through $7F80 after the swap: the right-hand counterpart of layout_left.
98 character codes, a 7 x 14 block that shop_draw_panel draws at row 6, column 8 ($44F8), read through $7F98: the witch's figure, under her sprites.

Six sprite colours for the three Magic Potion Creatures in the shop's top panel (shop_raster_top reads them through $7FFA): shop_init writes the loaded level's colours for the three kinds from $8CE2 over the first three ($EB6D); the other three are black, the outlines.
JMP shop_init. The engine jumps here ($BE5F) once a level's file has loaded, unless it is a torture chamber or the ending, so that the shop comes before every level.

The colour of each of the shop's 256 characters, to $E602: shop_draw_panel and shop_box_put write a character's colour to colour RAM from here. Once the panels are drawn, bytes here also serve as variables (shop_weapons, the gargoyles' frames, the flags at $E51D and $E539-$E53D); the box characters ($1B-$1F, $20, $25, $FE, $FF) keep their colours. The engine's JMP $E503 ($BE62, $1CD4) is meant for the attract block, which has a JMP here.

The player's own weapons while the shop runs: shop_init copies owned_weapons here (eleven bytes, the $FF end mark included) before filling owned_weapons with every item for sale; a purchase adds a new weapon at $CFE2's place ($EE3F); shop_leave rebuilds owned_weapons from it. These are the colours of characters $01-$0B, which the panels have used by then.
shop_weapons plus one: a purchase writes the $FF end mark after a new weapon through it ($EE44).
A random number for each of the two animated gargoyle cells (shop_eye_step): each new run makes it 5 x n + $81 (plus a carry), with bit 4 flipped.
The character for column 1 (and 36) of screen row 2 at each of the five frames of shop_eye_step: $6D (as drawn), $00, $2A, $2A, $00.
The character for column 3 (and 38) at each frame: $70 (as drawn), $22, $2B, $2B, $22.

Set by a $FE in a printed message (shop_print_step); while it is 1, shop_raster_witch_low starts the weapons tablet opening (tablet_close_setup, $124A = 1) and moves it to 2. The INGREDIENTS line starts with $FE, so the tablet opens as that line begins. The colour bytes after it are those of the boxes' corners and edges.
The colour for each of shop_eye_step's five frames: $0D, $0D, $08, $08, $0D.
Steps, one every other frame from $18, while the opened tablet rises a pixel a step; at 0 shop_frame shows the middle item (shop_show_item).
Each gargoyle cell's frame, counted down by shop_eye_step: frames 0-4 draw, 5 and above leave the cell alone.
Set to 7 by a purchase: on every other frame it counts down and the tablet's colours take the next step of the flash (flash_mc0, flash_mc1, flash_sprites); at 0 they return to flash_rest.
The text box shop_box_step is opening, 0-2.
200 character codes, the top five rows of the screen (the ornate top panel and the gargoyles' heads), which shop_draw_panel draws at $4400.
24 character codes, a 6 x 4 block drawn at row 5, column 0 ($44C8).
12 character codes, a 4 x 3 block drawn at row 13, column 4 ($460C).
20 character codes, a 4 x 5 block drawn at row 13, column 15 ($4617).
200 character codes, the bottom five rows ($4720): the panels round the weapons tablet and the item's name. It ends at $E7CA.
The bottom rows' layout from its 59th byte. The label is the engine's: the high-score page's raster routine calls $E73D ($F6EC), a routine of the attract block that sits here when the shop is not in.
The bottom rows' layout from its 111th byte. The label is the engine's: $C978 jumps to $E771 in the attract block.
The bottom rows' layout from its 175th byte: columns 14 to 39 of its last row, which shop_draw_panel copies with the rest.

Inverts the 80 bytes of characters $30-$39, the shop's digits, at $5980. shop_raster_witch_top calls it at line $5A and shop_raster_tablet again at line $CA, so the digits between those lines (the ingredients' costs) show in inverse and those above and below (the potion counts, the item's grade) do not.

Raster routine at line $5A: the first eight witch sprites, positions from witch_top_xy, pointers $EC-$F3 (witch_top_frames) and colours from witch_top_colours; multicolour for sprites 4-7, sprite multicolours orange and light red; then, after a short wait, background colours mid grey ($D022) and black ($D021), and the digits inverted (digits_invert). Next: shop_raster_witch_low at line $8A.

Raster routine at line $8A: background light red; the other eight witch sprites, from witch_low_xy, pointers $F4-$FB and witch_low_colours; multicolour for sprites 0, 1, 4, 5 and 6, sprite multicolour 2 brown, sprite 7 doubled in width. Then the shop's work done in the interrupt: the next character of a message while one prints (shop_print_step); the tablet's opening when tablet_trigger is 1; and at step 4 of a tablet turn ($1251), when the first channel's requested effect is $10, the effect requests cleared ($1260-$1265) and the new middle item shown (shop_show_item). Next: shop_raster_tablet at line $CA.
Raster routine at line $CA: background colours for the bottom panels, the weapons tablet's eight sprites (panel_sprites_tablet), and the digits put back. Next: shop_raster_frame at line $F4.

Raster routine at line $F4, and the chain's first: points all eight sprites at block $0F, adds one to the frame flag $120D and moves frame_divider's flags on ($1219 every frame, $121A every second, $121B every fourth), then after a wait sets the background colours for the top panel. Next: shop_raster_top at line 0.

Raster routine at line 0: the three Magic Potion Creatures of the top panel, each two sprites (frames $B6 and $B7, $B8 and $B9, $BA and $BB of the level's sprites) at potion_xy with potion_sprite_colours, all multicolour, sprite multicolours dark grey and yellow; and the music, through music_frame while music_on is set. Next: shop_raster_witch_top at line $5A.

Shows item A (0 EXIT, 1-8 the weapons, 9 INFORMATION) in the bottom panels. Unless the middle item's count in weapons_flags is 3 or more (a weapon bought to grade C, or EXIT, whose count is 4), with INFORMATION always priced, it colours the cost row yellow and writes the three costs, two digits each, at $466E, $4672 and $4676 from item_cost_1-3; otherwise it blanks them (costs_clear). Then the item's name from item_names (through item_names_lo/hi) at $4787, converted by shop_screen_code.
The low bytes of the ten items' names, by item number: $EA42 (EXIT), then $E9BB to $EA33 every 15 bytes.
The high bytes of the item names.

The ten names, 15 bytes each with a $00 at the end: "DROOPY      :", "SUPER DROOPY:", "FIREBALL    :", "FALL UP     :", "WIGGLER     :", "CURLY WURLY :", "FLAMER      :", "SCATTER BALL:" (each followed by the grade on offer, a screen code A to C, or a space once bought to grade C), "INFORMATION   " and "EXIT          ".
The low bytes of the grade letter in each weapon's name ($E9C8, $E9D7 ... $EA31): shop_init and a purchase write the next grade there.
The high bytes of the grade letters.

What each item costs in Magic Potion Creatures of the first kind, in decimal, by item less one: Droopy 0, Super Droopy 2, Fireball 2, Fall Up 3, Wiggler 2, Curly Wurly 3, Flamer 6, Scatter Ball 3, Information 6.
The costs in creatures of the second kind: 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.
The costs in creatures of the third kind: 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6.

The weapons tablet's eight sprite positions while the shop runs (x, y pairs, 16 bytes): shop_init exchanges them with tablet_sprite_xy, so that the tablet sits at the bottom left, and the exit swaps them back after setting each y here to $F4, so that the tablet always rises from the bottom.
The tablet's second sprite's position. The label is the engine's: its $1111 jumps to the KERNAL's $EA7E, with the ROM banked in.
The three icons' positions within shop_tablet_xy: shop_init writes each icon's x from the game's tablet less $50 ($EB9D).
Writes the counts of the three kinds of Magic Potion Creature ($B8A0-$B8A2), two white digits each, into the top panel at $445E, $4465 and $446C (potion_count_draw).
Draws the count X of potion kind X as two screen-code digits at $445E + Y.

The witch's shop. Blanks the screen, silences the sound, clears the frame flag and the sprite expansions, fills the screen with character $FD in colour 8, selects VIC bank 1 and swaps memory: 2 (shop_sprites to $7B00), 6 (the level's character set to $D000) and 1 (the shop's character set from $D800 into $5800). It takes three of its messages from the level ($8EF2/$8EF8, its message 3, as the second line; $8EF4/$8EFA, message 5, as the third clue) and the second clue from $9880 (or $9908 from stage 7); draws the seven screen panels; sets the joystick branch at $1E21 to BNE, so that the tablet turns with fire released; picks the greeting by Clyde's lives (0: the level's message 0; below $8EFB: message 2; otherwise message 1); copies the potion creatures' colours from $8CE2; lists every item on the tablet (owned_weapons from f_259E, the player's own kept in shop_weapons); writes each weapon's grade letter; points tablet_icon_colours at the purchase counts ($CFE3) instead of the grades; and starts its raster chain with shop_raster_frame. Then the main loop, once a frame.
Operand of the JSR at $EACB. The label is the engine's: $C988 reads a table at $EACC in the attract block.
The STA that clears the frame flag. The label is the engine's: $C991 reads colours from $EACE in the attract block.
High byte of the STA's operand at $EACE. The label is the engine's: $C99A reads a table at $EAD0 in the attract block.

Operand of the STA at $EAD1 (the label is the engine's, read at $C9A3 in the attract block), then the rest of the clearing: both sprite expansions, the box number, the print delay and the three effect priorities; the sprites zeroed, the screen filled with $FD in colour 8, bank 1, and memory swaps 2 and 6.
The LDX #1 before memory_swap 1. The label is the engine's: $C9D3 reads $EAFC in the attract block.
The JSR memory_swap. The label is the engine's: $C9CA reads $EAFE in the attract block.
High byte of the JSR's operand at $EAFE. The label is the engine's: $C9C1 reads a table at $EB00 in the attract block.

Operand of the LDA at $EB01 (the label is the engine's, read at $C9B8 in the attract block). From here shop_init copies the level's message 3 (the second line) and message 5 (the third clue) into message_lo/hi, and picks the second clue by the stage: $9908 from stage 7 ($12A2), $9880 before.
Draws the seven panels, 6 down to 0 (shop_draw_panel), the panel number kept in the operand of the LDX at $EB38.
Operand of the LDX at $EB38: the panel number. After the last panel: clear_sprites_43, the boxes' counts from box_start, the BNE into $1E21, and the greeting chosen by lives.
$D0 (BNE) into $1E21, the branch on the fire flag in weapons_tablet: in the shop the joystick turns the tablet without fire, and fire held sets $CFEE, the shop's signal to buy.
The greeting: message 0 with no lives left, 2 below the level's shop_lives_mark, 1 otherwise. The BIT at $EB5C hides the LDX #2 that the lower count takes.
$2C, a BIT absolute that swallows the LDX #2 after it, so that X stays 1 for the greeting when Clyde has at least the level's shop_lives_mark lives.

LDX #2, the greeting for fewer lives than the mark. Then the greeting's address from the level's shop_text_lo/hi into message 0, the three potion kinds' colours from $8CE2 into potion_sprite_colours, and item_show_delay set to $18.

Saves the player's weapons in shop_weapons and puts every item in owned_weapons: Droopy stays at place 0, and add_weapon_fallthrough's tail ($C8C6) copies places 1-10 from f_259E (weapons $58-$5E, INFORMATION $FC, EXIT $FD and the end mark), the place kept in the operand of the LDX at $EB8D. Then ten items, the tablet filled from place 9.

Operand of the LDX at $EB8D: the place in owned_weapons being copied. Then ten items on the tablet ($12A6) filled from place 9; the icons' x from the game's tablet less $50 into shop_icon_xy; each weapon's grade letter; tablet_icon_colours pointed at weapons_flags; the tablet's positions exchanged with shop_tablet_xy; the potion counts drawn; all sprites on, the music, tablet and flash flags cleared, message_done set; and the raster chain started at shop_raster_frame, with $01 = $35 (RAM and I/O, no ROMs) and carry set for the handler that saves its own registers.
The grade letter on offer in each weapon's name: its count in weapons_flags plus one (A to C), or a space after grade C.
$CFE3 into the LDA at $B3EF, so that the tablet's icons take their colours from the purchase counts while the shop runs.
The shop's main loop: waits for the frame flag, then runs shop_frame until EXIT is chosen.
LDA #1, BNE: the loop leaves for shop_leave once EXIT has been chosen; shop_init stores 0 in the operand and shop_buy adds one.
Operand of the LDA at $EC2C: set by shop_buy when the item is EXIT.

Leaves the shop: blanks the screen, silences the sound, turns the sprites off and clears the screen; puts the tablet's positions back (its y in shop_tablet_xy set to $F4 first) and the operand at $B3F0 back to weapon_grades ($B419); rebuilds owned_weapons from shop_weapons, the count in $CFE2; swaps memory back (1, 6, then 2), starts the level (level_begin) and goes to the Get Ready screen.

The shop's work each frame. The weapons tablet: while it opens ($124A positive) tablet_open moves it; once it is open ($124A negative), on every other frame it rises a pixel while item_show_delay counts down, and the middle item is shown when that reaches 0; tablet_close runs while $124C is set; and the joystick turns it (weapons_tablet), fire buying the middle item (shop_buy) once per press. Then the tune restarts if it has ended (shop_tune_start), and on every other frame the message boxes (shop_box_step), the two gargoyle cells (shop_eye_step) and any flash after a purchase move on.

The tablet is open: weapons_tablet reads the joystick, $CFEE cleared first so that it shows whether fire is held; unless the tablet is flashing, every third frame the icons' colours are set (tablet_icon_colours) and copied into flash_rest.
Fire held: shop_buy, which acts once until fire is released ($EDAB cleared).
The shop tune restarts whenever it has stopped (music_on clear).

The flash after a purchase: buy_flash counts down on every other frame, each step's colours read at the count less one from flash_mc0, flash_mc1 and flash_sprites (an $FF leaves that colour); at 0 the colours return to flash_rest, $ED9B and $ED9C.

The tablet sprites' multicolour 2 ($24EA's operand) at each step of the flash, 6 down to 0. The three flash tables overlap, each a byte on from the last, so one ramp of colours (black, blue, light blue, cyan, light green, white) passes through the sprites' own colour, multicolour 1 and multicolour 2 in turn, and the last step is all white.
The colour of all eight tablet sprites at each step of the flash: flash_mc1 read a byte on.
The tablet sprites' multicolour 1 ($24E5's operand) at each step: flash_mc1 read two bytes on, so the first step's $FF leaves it alone.
The tablet sprites' colours outside a flash, eight bytes: shop_frame copies the three icons' current colours into $ED95-$ED97 every third frame.
The three icons' colours within flash_rest, refreshed every third frame while the tablet is up: $00, $0D, $01 in this snapshot.
Sprite multicolour 1 after the flash, $0B.
Sprite multicolour 2 after the flash, $0F.
X = the middle icon's place in owned_weapons: the place before $12A5 (the right icon's), 9 when that wraps. With every item listed, that is the item less one, EXIT being 9.
Ends a purchase: back to binary mode and redraw the potion counts (potions_show).

Fire on the middle item. Nothing while $EDAB says this press has already bought. EXIT sets shop_exit_flag. Otherwise each of the three potion counts must reach the item's cost (decimal compares, item_cost_1-3), or nothing happens. A weapon already at grade C is refused; otherwise its count in weapons_flags rises, the name's grade letter moves on (a space and blanked costs after grade C) and the item is shown again; a weapon new to the player joins shop_weapons at grade index 0, and one already owned goes up a grade (weapon_grades). INFORMATION, while no message is printing and fewer than three clues have been bought since the last chamber ($CFED below 5), clears the message box (box size 0) and prints the next clue (message $CFED: 3, 4 or 5). Either way the costs are then taken from the three counts and their sum from the total ($B89F), and the tablet flashes (buy_flash 7).
Operand of the LDA at $EDAA: set once a press has bought, cleared by shop_frame when fire is released.
The decimal comparisons of the three potion counts with the item's costs.
The middle item's count in weapons_flags plus one; INFORMATION (X 8) goes on at buy_item_kind, and a weapon whose count would pass 3 is refused.
Adds one to the grade letter in the weapon's name; after grade C a space is written instead ($EDFA).
The item's sprite frame from f_259E: a weapon ($57-$5E) or INFORMATION ($FC, negative).
The BPL that sends a weapon to $EE32; INFORMATION goes on here.
A weapon: if it is in shop_weapons its grade goes up, otherwise it is added at the end with grade 0 and an $FF after it.
The payment: buy_flash 7, the three costs subtracted in decimal, and their sum subtracted from the total through the SBC's operand.
Operand of the SBC at $EE8F: the item's three costs added together, written at $EE88.
Fills the cost row with the background character $FE ($466E-$4677).

Animates gargoyle cell Y (0 left, 1 right) on screen row 2. While its frame (eye_timers) is above 0 it counts down; at 0 a new random number (eye_seeds) gives the next count, doubled until it is 5 or more. Frames 0-4 write eye_frames_left and eye_frames_right at columns 1 and 3 (36 and 38 for the right) in eye_colours, so each cell plays its five frames backwards and then rests for a random time. A 0 would make the doubling loop for ever, but only seeds $83 and $B6 lead to 0 and no seed leads to them.

Runs the shop's three messages in turn, a step every other frame. Box box_number's count (box_count) falls by one; below box_wait the box is drawn a size larger at each step (shop_draw_box, size = count less box_base, so the frame grows as the count falls), and at box_text_at the message starts (shop_message) and the count is set to 0. Once that message has printed (message_done) the next starts: 0 the greeting, which zooms the box open; 1 the second line, which clears the box and prints over it; 2 INGREDIENTS, in its own box below.
The three boxes' starting counts, copied to box_count by shop_init: $19, $37, $19.
The counts of the three boxes; 0 is done. The fourth byte ($B1) is never used as one.
The count below which each box draws: 9, $0B, $10.
The count at which each box's message starts: 0, 9, $0A.
What is taken from the count to find the box size: 0, 9, 1. Box 0 draws sizes 8 down to 1, box 1 size 1 once, box 2 sizes 14 down to 10.
Starts the shop's tune at $F300 (music_play).
The low bytes of the seven screen panels' layouts (shop_draw_panel, panel X): $E603, $E6CB, $7F80, $7F98, $E6E3, $E6EF, $E703.
Their high bytes; panels 2 and 3 read the witch's layouts through the sprite bank, $7F80 and $7F98, after memory_swap 2.
The high bytes of each panel's place on the screen ($4400-$47E7).
Each panel's width in characters: 40, 6, 6, 7, 4, 4, 40.
Each panel's height in rows: 5, 4, 4, 14, 3, 5, 5.

Copies panel X's layout to the screen a row at a time, with each character's colour from shop_char_colours into colour RAM ($94 pages above the screen row), the rows left kept in the operand of the LDX at $EFB2.
Operand of the LDX at $EFB2: the rows left to copy, counted down to the end of the panel.

The shop's 16 box sizes (shop_draw_box, X): the high byte of each size's top left corner on the screen. Sizes 0 and 1 are the full message box, 19 x 6 characters at row 6, column 17; 2-9 shrink towards row 8, column 25 (the message box grows through 8 down to 1); 10-15 are the INGREDIENTS box at row 13, column 20, and smaller.
The low byte of each size's top left corner.
Each size's width less one: the column of its right edge, from $12 down to 2.
Each size's height in rows, 6 down to 2.
Each size's colour: 9 for the message box, $0F for the INGREDIENTS box.

Draws box size X: its rows filled with the blank character $FE in the box's colour, then the frame: top corners $1B and $1C with the top edge $1F, sides $20 and $25, bottom corners $1D and $1E with the bottom edge $FF, each in its colour from shop_char_colours.
Operand of the LDX at $F054: the rows left to fill.
Operand of the LDX at $F085: the side rows left to draw.
Draws one horizontal edge: the corner A at the left, the corner Y (into $F0A1) at the right and the edge character X (into $F0A9) between.
Operand of the LDA at $F0A0: the right-hand corner, written by box_edge from Y.
Operand of the LDA at $F0A8: the edge character, written by box_edge from X, repeated between the corners.
Puts character A at (screen),Y and its colour from shop_char_colours at (colour RAM),Y.

The low bytes of the shop's six messages (shop_message, Y): 0 the greeting and 1 the second line (both from the level, written by shop_init), 2 "INGREDIENTS:" ($F15D), 3 the first clue at $8F0D, 4 the second ($9880, or $9908 from stage 7), 5 the third (from the level).
Message 1's low byte, then messages 2 and 3: shop_init writes message 1 from the level's message 3, the second line.
Message 4's low byte, the second clue: $80 ($9880) before stage 7, $08 ($9908) from it.
Message 5's low byte, the third clue, from the level's message 5.
The high bytes of the six messages.
Message 1's high byte, then messages 2 and 3.
Message 4's high byte: $98 before stage 7, $99 from it.
Message 5's high byte.
The high byte of each message's first screen position: $45 for all but INGREDIENTS ($46).
The low byte: $452A for the messages in the box, $4644 for INGREDIENTS.
The place in the message line being printed (Y of shop_print_step).
0 while a message prints, 1 when none is printing; shop_buy prints a clue only when it is 1, and shop_box_step starts the next message only then.
Starts message Y: its text address into $C6/$C7, its screen address into $C8/$C9 and the colour RAM's into $CA/$CB, and printing on (message_done 0).
Frames to the next character, 2 down to 0: a character every third frame.

Prints the next character of the message, every third frame (from shop_raster_witch_low). $00 ends the message (message_done); $FF starts the next line, 40 characters down, the text pointer moved past the line; $FE sets tablet_trigger and leaves a blank; any other byte goes on the screen as a screen code (shop_screen_code), its colour RAM byte lowered by 8 so that the letter is drawn in one colour rather than multicolour.
Operand of the ADC at $F124: the line's length plus one, written at $F11E.
Turns an ASCII byte into the shop's screen code: a space becomes the background character $FE, letters ($41 and up) lose $40, other bytes stay.
$FE, "INGREDIENTS:" and $00: message 2. Its $FE opens the weapons tablet as it prints.
The x and y of the six potion sprites in the top panel: three at y $38 (x $6C, $A4, $DC) and their outlines one pixel right and down.
The six potion sprites' frames: $B6, $B8, $BA, then $B7, $B9, $BB.
The x and y of the first eight witch sprites (shop_raster_witch_top).
Their frames, $EC-$F3.
Their colours: brown for the first four, light grey for the multicolour four laid over them.
The x and y of the other eight witch sprites (shop_raster_witch_low).
Their frames, $F4-$FB.
Their colours: light grey, light grey, brown, brown, then light grey three times (as $9F) and dark grey.
67 bytes to the end of the file at $F1FF that nothing reads, laid out like rows of a sprite's shape, three bytes to a row.
